reuse.why: Routes the three weekend call sites through a new shared getDateWithWeekendRule, but leaves the old getDateWithSkippedWeekend exported and unused instead of evolving it, and the new handler only partly reuses the shared rule.

duplication.why: The old getDateWithSkippedWeekend survives alongside the new rule function, the daily weekend/holiday skip is written separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange, and getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' RSchedule pipeline.

placement.why: The move rule sits in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip part of the same rule lives at call sites (getNextDate loop, getDatesInRange flatMap) rather than in the shared definition.

scope.why: Edits stay within schedule date code, the budget template consumer and the type; the inline type cast for holidays is a small wart.

maintainability.why: The weekend rule is split between a shared helper, a string wrapper and two call-site daily/holiday checks, with holidays not passed at every site, so a future rule change still needs several edits.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) decide the daily weekend/holiday skip themselves before calling getDateWithWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: getDateWithWeekendRule re-expresses the left-in-place getDateWithSkippedWeekend as a day-by-day loop; the daily skip check is reshaped as a while/continue in getNextDate and a flatMap guard in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithWeekendRule gains a holidays parameter; the daily-schedule skip is kept out of it and re-implemented at getNextDate and getDatesInRange.
